summary:
The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 modifies bankruptcy trustee compensation, chapter 11 quarterly fee funding, and the duration of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships.

Section 3 amends 11 U.S.C. § 330(b)(1) to increase the per-case compensation payable to trustees serving in chapter 7 cases from $45 to $105, leaving the additional $15 payment under § 330(b)(2) unaffected, and repeals 11 U.S.C. § 330(e). It also prescribes, notwithstanding any other law, the allocation of the remainder of fees collected under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(1)(A) after payment of § 330(b)(1) trustee compensation: $63.51 to the special fund under 28 U.S.C. § 1931, $25.00 to the special fund established under § 10101(b) of the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005, and $51.49 to the United States Trustee System Fund under 28 U.S.C. § 589a. Section 3 further amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(b)(1)(A) to replace the current percentage allocation of certain fees with a fixed $51.49 per case allocation, and amends § 589a(f)(1) by eliminating two subparagraphs and redesignating the remaining priority language.

Section 4 amends 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6)(B), governing quarterly fees in chapter 11 cases, by extending the applicable period from 5 years to 10 years and modifying the fee calculation to require the greater of the specified 0.4 percent amount or the amount determined under the amended alternative formula, which is increased from 0.8 percent to 0.9 percent. It amends 28 U.S.C. § 589a(f) to extend references from 2026 to 2031. For fiscal years 2026 through 2031, notwithstanding § 589a(b), fees collected under § 1930(a)(6), less $5,400,000, must be deposited as specified in § 589a(f), while $5,400,000 must be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury.

Section 5 amends § 4 of the Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2020 and § 1003(b)(2)(A) of the Bankruptcy Judgeship Act of 2017, both codified as notes to 28 U.S.C. § 152, to extend specified temporary bankruptcy judgeship offices from 5 years to 10 years.

Section 6 provides that, except as otherwise specified, the Act’s amendments take effect on the first day of the calendar quarter first occurring on or after enactment. Section 3 applies to chapter 7 cases commenced on or after the first October 1 after enactment, and to chapter 11, 12, or 13 cases commenced on or after that date that are converted to chapter 7. Section 4 applies to chapter 11 cases commenced or pending on the first day of the relevant calendar quarter and to quarterly fees under 28 U.S.C. § 1930(a)(6) for disbursements made in calendar quarters beginning on or after enactment.
